nodes.summary: Non-explosion (Norris 1997, §2.7, for a finite state space): almost surely the jump times of the chain started at `i` tend to `∞`, so `X t` is a genuine state of the jump chain for every `t ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Non-explosion

nodes.summary: The holding times of the shifted steps started at `Y n` are the holding times after `n`.
nodes.title: Holding times of the shifted steps

nodes.summary: The `n`-th holding time `S n = E n / q (Y n)`, where `q k = -Q k k`; it is `∞` when `Y n` is absorbing (`q (Y n) = 0`). Negative clock values, a null event, give `S n = 0`.
nodes.title: Holding times of a continuous-time Markov chain

nodes.summary: Strong Markov property at jump times (Norris 1997, §2.6–2.7): let `A` be a measurable set of histories of the first `n` steps such that `T n < ∞` whenever the history lies in `A`; these histories determine `Y 0, …, Y n` and `S 0, …, S (n - 1)`. Then for every state `k` and every measurable set `B` of paths, the path after `T n` is independent of the event `{history ∈ A, Y n = k}` and distributed as the chain…
nodes.title: Strong Markov property at jump times

nodes.summary: Restart law at a fixed time (cf. the Markov property, Norris 1997, §2.8), for events of `X s` and of the path after `s` only: for the chain started at `i`, the probability that `X s = k` and that the path after `s` lies in a measurable set `B` is `exp (s Q) i k` times the probability that the chain started at `k` lies in `B`. This is weaker than the Markov property with respect to the natural filtration: arbitrary…
nodes.title: Restart law at a fixed time

nodes.summary: Kolmogorov (Norris 1997, §2.8, Theorem 2.8.2 for a finite state space): the chain built from the jump chain and the holding times has transition function `exp (t • Q)`: `P_i(X t = j) = exp (t Q) i j` for every `t ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Kolmogorov

nodes.summary: Finite-dimensional distributions (Norris 1997, §2.8, Theorem 2.8.2 (c)): with increments `s 0, …, s (n - 1) ≥ 0`, times `t k = s 0 + ⋯ + s k`, and states `j 0, …, j (n - 1)`, `P_i(X (t k) = j k for all k) = ∏ₖ exp (s k Q) (j (k - 1)) (j k)`, where `j (-1) = i`.
nodes.title: Finite-dimensional distributions

nodes.summary: The law of the i.i.d. step sequence `ω : ℕ → (ι → ι) × ℝ` driving the chain.
nodes.title: Law of the driving step sequence of a Markov chain

nodes.summary: The jump chain of the shifted steps started at `Y n` is the jump chain after `n`.
nodes.title: Jump chain of the shifted steps

nodes.summary: The jump chain started at `i`: `Y 0 = i` and `Y (n + 1) = ξ n (Y n)`.
nodes.title: Jump chain of a continuous-time Markov chain

nodes.summary: The jump matrix of a rate matrix is row-stochastic.
nodes.title: Jump matrix is row-stochastic

nodes.summary: The entries of the jump matrix of a rate matrix are nonnegative.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the jump matrix

nodes.summary: The jump matrix `Π` of a matrix `Q` (Norris 1997, §2.6): for a state with exit rate `q i = -Q i i ≠ 0`, `Π i j = Q i j / q i` for `j ≠ i` and `Π i i = 0`; a state with `q i = 0` is absorbing, `Π i j = δ i j`.
nodes.title: Jump matrix of a rate matrix

nodes.summary: Row `i` of the jump matrix of a rate matrix, as a probability mass function on `ι`.
nodes.title: Row of the jump matrix as a probability mass function

nodes.summary: `T (n + m) = T n + T' m`, where `T'` are the jump times of the shifted steps started at `Y n`.
nodes.title: Additivity of jump times under shifting

nodes.summary: The jump times are nondecreasing.
nodes.title: Jump times are nondecreasing

nodes.summary: The `n`-th jump time `T n = S 0 + ⋯ + S (n - 1)`, with `T 0 = 0`.
nodes.title: Jump times of a continuous-time Markov chain

nodes.summary: First-jump decomposition of the path: before the first holding time the chain is at `i`; afterwards it is the chain started at `ξ 0 i` driven by the shifted steps.
nodes.title: First-jump decomposition

nodes.summary: If `T n ≤ t < T (n + 1)`, then `X t = Y n`.
nodes.title: Path value between consecutive jump times

nodes.summary: After a finite jump time `T n`, the path is the path started at `Y n` driven by the shifted steps: `X (T n + s) = X' s` with `X'` built from `shift n ω` started at `Y n`.
nodes.title: Path restarts at a jump time

nodes.summary: The path of the chain started at `i`: `X t = Y n` for the `n` with `T n ≤ t < T (n + 1)`. If `t` is at or after the explosion time `sup T n` (a null event, by `IsRateMatrix.ae_tendsto_ctmcJumpTime`), the value is an arbitrary state that does not depend on `i`, `Q` or `ω`.
nodes.title: Path of a continuous-time Markov chain

nodes.summary: The shift of the step sequence by `n`: `(shift n ω) m = ω (n + m)`.
nodes.title: Shift of the step sequence of a Markov chain

nodes.summary: The law of one step `(ξ, E)` of the construction: `ξ : ι → ι` has independent coordinates with `ξ i ∼ Π i`, and `E` is an independent exponential clock of rate `1`.
nodes.title: Law of one step of the chain construction

nodes.summary: The holding time `S n` is a measurable function of the steps.
nodes.title: Measurability of the holding times

nodes.summary: The jump chain `Y n` is a measurable function of the steps.
nodes.title: Measurability of the jump chain

nodes.summary: The jump time `T n` is a measurable function of the steps.
nodes.title: Measurability of the jump times

nodes.summary: The path `(t, ω) ↦ X t` is jointly measurable in the time and the steps.
nodes.title: Joint measurability of the chain path in time and steps

nodes.summary: The state `X t` is a measurable function of the steps.
nodes.title: Measurability of the chain state at a fixed time

nodes.summary: The rows of the jump matrix of a rate matrix sum to `1`.
nodes.title: Rows of the jump matrix sum to one
